items.q: Programmatic advertising means ads are bought and sold by software, often in real time.
items.why: Software handles the buying and selling, instead of people agreeing each deal by hand.

items.q: In a second-price auction the winner pays just above the second-highest bid.
items.why: The winner pays less than they bid unless there was no close competitor.

items.q: OpenRTB is a standard way for buyers and sellers to describe bids and requests.
items.why: A shared standard lets many different systems talk to each other.

items.q: A bid request describes the impression and sometimes the page and the user.
items.why: Buyers use that information to decide whether and how much to bid.

items.q: Programmatic buying always costs less than buying directly.
items.why: Prices depend on demand, fees and the quality of the inventory.

items.q: A private marketplace is open to every buyer.
items.why: It is invite-only, so only chosen buyers can bid.

items.q: A programmatic auction usually finishes in a fraction of a second.
items.why: It happens while the page loads, so the visitor does not wait.

items.q: A deal ID links a buyer and a seller’s agreed terms inside the auction systems.
items.why: It tells both platforms which agreement an impression belongs to.
